name: DNS & Web Recon
description: DNS-tunneling, DGA and web reconnaissance signals. Combines DNS query patterns with HTTP host, user-agent and status-code distributions to expose suspicious browsing.

charts.title: Top DNS Queries
charts.description: Most-queried hostnames in the capture. Random-looking subdomains, very long names, or repeated odd lookups suggest DGA-driven malware or DNS-tunneled exfiltration.

charts.title: DNS Response Codes
charts.description: Distribution of DNS response codes. A high share of NXDOMAIN responses is a classic indicator of beaconing or DGA-based C2 looking for its rendezvous domain.

charts.title: DNS Query Name Entropy
charts.description: Shannon entropy of query names over time. Sustained high entropy points to encoded payloads carried inside DNS labels (tunneling, exfil).

charts.title: HTTP Hosts Contacted
charts.description: Most-contacted HTTP hosts. Unfamiliar or low-reputation hosts deserve a pivot into Connection / TLS detail and a check against threat-intel feeds.

charts.title: HTTP User Agents
charts.description: Top User-Agent strings. Outliers like curl, wget, python-requests, Go-http-client or custom strings frequently indicate automation, scanners or malware.

charts.title: HTTP Status Codes
charts.description: HTTP status code distribution. A spike in 401/403/404 responses typically means credential probing, path enumeration or an actively-scanning attacker.
